html:
Tuol Sleng was a high school in Phnom Penh that the Khmer Rouge turned into Security Prison 21 (S-21). From 1976 to 1979 well over 12,000 people were held and tortured there; only a handful survived.

Most prisoners were Khmer Rouge cadres accused of treason as the regime turned on itself. Guards photographed each prisoner and forced written confessions, then took them to be killed at Choeung Ek, one of the killing fields.

The Vietnamese found the prison in 1979 and opened it as a museum. Its records were key evidence at the tribunal that convicted its chief, Duch, in 2010, and later senior leaders of genocide. See Pol Pot and Cambodian genocide.
